newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss give Bosnian refugees until April to leave.
newsitem.headline: Swiss give Bosnian refugees until April to leave.

text.p: Switzerland on Wednesday gave thousands of Bosnian refugees on its soil until the end of April to leave, saying those failing to comply with the deadline could face expulsion, the Swiss news agency ATS reported.
But the Federal Council, or cabinet, made an exception for minors and refugee families with children at a meeting in Berne, and allowed them to stay in the country until April 1988.

Switzerland hosts up to 18,000 refugees from former Yugoslavia, whose disintegration in 1991 touched off ethnic war among Serbs, Croats and Moslems. Their requests for asylum have been rejected, Swiss officials said.

Among them some 8,000 refugees will have to leave the country by April, ATS said. Those refusing to do so will lose a third of their financial state aid and be sent home by force if necessary by 2000, it quoted a cabinet decision as saying.

More than a year after the U.S.-brokered Dayton peace accord ended 43 months of war in Bosnia, only 250,000 of the 2.1 million uprooted Bosnians have returned home, despite the right to return being central to the peace treaty.

Most are blocked from returning or are unwilling to go home because ethnic intolerance and harassment continues, mainly in Serb and Croat areas, despite efforts by the international community to put a stop to it.
Germany took in 320,000 refugees, more than any other country outside former Yugoslavia. Some German states have begun a forced repatriation programme of Bosnian refugees.
